title: Rebilling Hold-Back When a Prior Authorization Approval Is Voided
content:
## Prior Authorization — units kept for rebilling of denied claims

**Rule.** The rebilling hold-back of a void of a Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization approval counts the member's claims denied for no prior authorization whose service dates fall within the two months before the day of the void (a date counts when fewer than two whole months separate it from that day): two or more such claims hold back 2 units, exactly one holds back 1 unit, and none holds back nothing.

The claims counted are the member's medical claims on the Medicaid Managed Care Membership claim ledger that were adjudicated as denied with the denial reason "no prior authorization"; each is placed in or out of the window by its service date.

The hold-back is a whole number of units, taken once from the units the voided approval left unused; the units released are never below zero.

### Input — judgement — output

| Such claims in the window | Judgement | Units held back |
|---|---|---|
| None | No claim awaits rebilling | 0 |
| Exactly 1 | One claim | 1 |
| 2, 3 or more | Two or more claims | 2 |

### Window boundary (hypothetical dates, for illustration only)

For a void on 15 September, a denied claim with a service date of 16 July is inside the window (fewer than two whole months before), and one with a service date of 15 July is outside it (two whole months before).

### Hypothetical cases, for illustration only

- One claim denied for no prior authorization five weeks before the void and one denied as a duplicate: only the first counts, **1 unit**.
- Four claims denied for no prior authorization, all within the window: **2 units**.
- A claim denied for no prior authorization three months before the void: outside the window, **nothing**.
